title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Work Guidance for the "One-Stop" Diversified Resolution Platform for International Commercial Disputes of the Supreme People's Court (Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Work Guidelines for the "One-Stop" International Commercial Dispute Diversified Resolution Platform of the Supreme People's Court (Trial)

Fa [2023] No. 247

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; all units of this Court:

For the purpose of thoroughly studying and implementing the important speech of General Secretary Xi Jinping on strengthening the construction of the foreign-related legal system, further implementing the Opinions of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council on Establishing a Mechanism and Institution for International Commercial Dispute Resolution for the Belt and Road Initiative, improving the "One-Stop" diversified resolution mechanism for international commercial disputes that organically connects litigation with mediation and arbitration, and facilitating parties to use the information-based platform to resolve international commercial disputes, the Supreme People's Court has formulated the Work Guidelines for the "One-Stop" International Commercial Dispute Diversified Resolution Platform of the Supreme People's Court (Trial) in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of the International Commercial Court, and other relevant laws and judicial interpretations. These Guidelines are hereby issued.

This Notice shall take effect on January 30, 2024.

December 22, 2023

Supreme People's Court

Work Guidelines for the "One-Stop" International Commercial Dispute Diversified Resolution Platform

(Trial)

For the purpose of facilitating parties to use the "One-Stop" International Commercial Dispute Diversified Resolution Platform of the Supreme People's Court to resolve international commercial disputes in a fair, efficient, and convenient manner, these Guidelines are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of the International Commercial Court, and other relevant laws and judicial interpretations.

Article 1 The "One-Stop" International Commercial Dispute Diversified Resolution Platform (hereinafter referred to as the "One-Stop" Platform) refers to the full-process online service platform established by the International Commercial Court of the Supreme People's Court on its official website (http://cicc.court.gov.cn), which is organically connected with the international commercial mediation institutions, international commercial arbitration institutions, and expert members of the International Commercial Expert Committee of the Supreme People's Court (hereinafter referred to as expert committee members) within the "One-Stop" international commercial dispute diversified resolution mechanism. It supports and facilitates parties to resolve international commercial disputes by selecting diversified methods such as neutral evaluation, mediation, arbitration, or litigation.

The "One-Stop" Platform sets up functions including "Mediation Service," "Arbitration Service," "Litigation Service," and "Auxiliary Service." It generates, sends, receives, stores, and exchanges relevant materials in accordance with the progress of the case process, and simultaneously sends the relevant materials and node information to the relevant parties, platform institutions, and expert committee members.

Article 2 In accordance with the provisions of Items 1, 3, and 4 of Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of the International Commercial Court, a party may apply through the "One-Stop" Platform for neutral evaluation, mediation, arbitration, or initiate litigation with respect to an international commercial dispute with a subject matter of RMB 300 million or more, or an international commercial dispute that otherwise has significant impact.

Article 3 A party that chooses to resolve an international commercial dispute through the "One-Stop" Platform shall fill in necessary information such as a mobile phone number or email address as prompted by the Platform and complete registration.

Article 4 Where a party applies for neutral evaluation before submitting to mediation, arbitration, or litigation, it shall select the neutral evaluation function under "Auxiliary Service" on the "One-Stop" Platform, fill in a neutral evaluation application form stating the expert committee member of its choice, and submit identity certification materials and relevant evidentiary materials.

After receiving the party's application materials for neutral evaluation, if the International Commercial Court considers that the dispute falls within the scope of application of Article 2 of these Guidelines, it shall, within three working days, solicit the opinion of the respondent on whether to agree to conduct the neutral evaluation. If the respondent agrees, it shall submit a written opinion agreeing to the neutral evaluation.

Article 5 After an expert committee member is selected as a neutral evaluator, he or she may, through the "One-Stop" Platform, convene an evaluation meeting, hear the statements of the parties, ask questions to the parties on matters related to the evaluation, and analyze and evaluate the validity of evidence, factual findings, application of law, etc., based on the statements of the parties and relevant evidence, and issue a neutral evaluation opinion. The period for neutral evaluation shall generally not exceed twenty working days. If all parties agree to extend the period for neutral evaluation, an appropriate extension may be granted.

Neutral evaluation shall not be conducted in public. The neutral evaluator shall keep confidential the information provided by the parties, and shall not disclose it to the other party without the permission of the party providing the information. The neutral evaluation opinion shall have no legal effect and may not be used as evidence in subsequent proceedings.

The parties may reach a settlement on their own based on the neutral evaluation opinion, or may apply for the expert committee member who participated in the evaluation to preside over mediation. The expert committee member who participated in the evaluation may conduct mediation in accordance with the provisions of these Guidelines but shall not participate in any other proceedings except mediation.

The fees for neutral evaluation shall be determined by the expert committee member and the parties through consultation.

Article 6 A party applying for mediation may, through the "Mediation Service" on the "One-Stop" Platform of the International Commercial Court, enter the "People's Court Mediation Platform" and log in to apply for mediation by an international commercial mediation institution or an expert committee member.

Mediation by an international commercial mediation institution shall be conducted in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and the mediation rules of that institution.

Mediation by an expert committee member shall be conducted in accordance with relevant laws and regulations, the Procedural Rules for the International Commercial Court of the Supreme People's Court (Trial), the Working Rules of the International Commercial Expert Committee of the Supreme People's Court (Trial), the Rules of the People's Court for Online Mediation, and these Guidelines.

Article 7 A party applying for mediation shall submit the following materials:

(1) A mediation application, stating the names or titles, addresses, telephone numbers, fax numbers, email addresses, and other contact information of all parties, the facts of the dispute, and the mediation requests;

(2) Relevant evidentiary materials;

(3) Identity certification materials;

(4) Where a lawyer or other person is entrusted to act as agent, the power of attorney and identity certification of the agent shall be submitted;

(5) Confirmation of Service Address and Method.

Article 8 After receiving the party's mediation application materials, if the International Commercial Court considers that the dispute falls within the scope of application of Article 2 of these Guidelines, it shall, within three working days, solicit the opinion of the respondent on whether to agree to mediation. If the respondent agrees, it shall submit a written opinion agreeing to mediation.

Article 9 Where a party has not applied for mediation, the International Commercial Court may inquire whether the party is willing to accept mediation referred by the court before filing the case. If the party has a willingness to mediate and indicates consent to pre-filing mediation in the Pre-trial Diversion Procedure Consultation Form, the International Commercial Court shall contact the relevant parties regarding the referral for mediation.

After the International Commercial Court accepts a case, if the parties have a willingness to mediate, the International Commercial Court shall contact the relevant parties regarding the entrustment of mediation.

Article 10 Where the International Commercial Court refers or entrusts mediation to an international commercial mediation institution, it shall, after the parties have selected or the International Commercial Court has designated the international commercial mediation institution, transfer the Pre-trial Diversion Procedure Consultation Form, the Letter of Inquiry on Referral/Entrustment of Mediation, and the relevant case materials to the corresponding institution.

The international commercial mediation institution shall reply within three working days after receiving the Letter of Inquiry on Referral/Entrustment of Mediation.

If the international commercial mediation institution accepts the selection or designation, the International Commercial Court shall, within three working days, issue the Letter of Referral/Entrustment of Mediation and notify the parties through the "One-Stop" Platform.

If the international commercial mediation institution fails to reply within the above-mentioned time limit, it shall be deemed not to accept the referral/entrustment of mediation.

Article 11 Where all parties agree to mediation by expert committee members, the International Commercial Court shall, within seven working days, organize the parties to jointly select one to three expert committee members from the list of expert committee members to serve as mediators.

The International Commercial Court shall promptly contact the selected expert committee member(s) to arrange and advance the relevant mediation work, and transfer the Pre-trial Diversion Procedure Consultation Form, the Letter of Inquiry on Referral/Entrustment of Mediation, and the relevant case materials to the corresponding expert committee member(s).

The expert committee member shall reply within seven working days after receiving the Letter of Inquiry on Referral/Entrustment of Mediation.

If the expert committee member accepts the selection, the International Commercial Court shall, within three working days, issue the Letter of Referral/Entrustment of Mediation and notify the parties through the "One-Stop" Platform.

If the expert committee member fails to reply within the above-mentioned time limit, it shall be deemed not to accept the referral/entrustment of mediation.

Article 12 Before presiding over mediation, an expert committee member shall sign a declaration guaranteeing independent and impartial mediation. If, when presiding over mediation, the expert committee member becomes aware of circumstances that may cause a party to have reasonable doubts as to the mediator's independence or impartiality, he or she shall promptly make a written disclosure to the International Commercial Court.

The International Commercial Court shall, within three working days after receiving the disclosure materials from the expert committee member, notify the parties through the "One-Stop" Platform.

Article 13 Where a party applies for the replacement of an expert committee member on the grounds of reasonable doubts as to the mediator's impartiality or independence, the party shall make a written application within three working days after becoming aware of the grounds for replacement or after receiving the disclosure materials from the expert committee member. If no application for replacement is made within the time limit, the right to apply shall be deemed waived.

The International Commercial Court shall, within three working days after receiving the party's written application, review the matter and decide whether to replace the expert committee member. During the review period, the mediation proceedings shall not be suspended.

Article 14 The period for mediation presided over by an expert committee member shall run from the date of acceptance of the referral/entrustment of mediation and shall generally not exceed twenty working days. If all parties agree to extend the mediation period, an appropriate extension may be granted.

Article 15 Mediation shall not be conducted in public. A record of the mediation proceedings shall be made and signed by the parties and the expert committee member or the mediator of the international commercial mediation institution who presided over the mediation.

The mediation record and facts acknowledged by the parties as concessions for the purpose of reaching a mediation agreement shall not be used as a basis adverse to the party in arbitration or litigation proceedings, unless otherwise provided by law or all parties agree.

Article 16 Where, after mediation presided over by an international commercial mediation institution or an expert committee member, the parties reach a mediation agreement, they shall sign a written mediation agreement.

Upon application by the parties, the International Commercial Court shall, in accordance with the law, review the mediation agreement and prepare a civil consent judgment; if the parties request the International Commercial Court to prepare a judgment, the International Commercial Court may prepare a civil judgment.

Article 17 During the mediation process, any of the following circumstances shall be deemed as failure to mediate:

(1) Any party requests in writing to terminate the mediation proceedings;

(2) The parties fail to reach a mediation agreement within the agreed mediation period, unless all parties agree to extend the mediation period;

(3) The international commercial mediation institution deems it inappropriate to continue mediation or terminates mediation for other reasons;

(4) An expert committee member is unable to perform, unable to continue to perform, or unsuitable to perform mediation duties and no other expert committee member can be selected;

(5) Other circumstances.

If the referral/entrustment of mediation fails, the international commercial mediation institution or the expert committee member shall, within three working days, return the Mediation Status Report and the relevant case materials to the International Commercial Court. After receiving the materials, the International Commercial Court shall promptly register the case; if the case has already been registered, it shall continue to proceed with the trial and notify the parties through the "One-Stop" Platform.

Article 18 Where a party voluntarily chooses to have mediation conducted by an international commercial mediation institution, the fee collection method and standards of that institution shall apply.

Where a party voluntarily chooses to have mediation conducted by an expert committee member, reference may be made to the fee collection method and standards of the international commercial mediation institutions on the "One-Stop" Platform.

Article 19 Where a party chooses to apply for arbitration through the "One-Stop" Platform, it may select an international commercial arbitration institution under "Apply for Arbitration" in the "Arbitration Service" and submit the relevant materials for arbitration application in accordance with the requirements of that institution.

Article 20 Where a party applies for preservation in arbitration, it may, through the "One-Stop" Platform under "Arbitration Service," select "Apply for Arbitration Preservation" and submit the following application materials to the international commercial arbitration institution:

(1) A written application for arbitration preservation;

(2) The arbitration agreement;

(3) Identity certification materials;

(4) Where a lawyer or other person is entrusted to act as agent, the power of attorney and identity certification of the agent shall be submitted;

(5) Relevant evidentiary materials;

(6) Documents related to the provision of security.

Article 21 An application for arbitration preservation shall state the following:

(1) The basic information, service address, and contact information of the applicant and the respondent;

(2) The specific request and the facts and reasons on which it is based;

(3) The amount of property, evidence, or subject matter of the dispute to be preserved;

(4) Clear information or specific leads regarding the property, evidence to be preserved;

(5) Information on property or credit standing provided as security for preservation, or reasons why the provision of security is not necessary;

(6) Whether an application has already been filed with another court;

(7) Other matters that need to be stated.

Article 22 After receiving the preservation application materials submitted by the party, if the international commercial arbitration institution, upon review, considers that the dispute falls within the scope of application of Article 2 of these Guidelines, it shall, through the "One-Stop" Platform, issue a letter of transmission to the International Commercial Court.

After receiving the letter of transmission and the arbitration preservation application materials, if the International Commercial Court considers that the dispute falls within the scope of application of Article 2 of these Guidelines, it shall register the case and render a ruling within five days. If the party needs to supplement preservation materials, the ruling shall be rendered within five days after the supplementation of the arbitration preservation application materials is completed; if the parties need to be questioned, the ruling shall be rendered within five days after the questioning.

If the International Commercial Court rules to take preservation measures, it may assign the execution to the people's court at the domicile of the respondent, the location of the property to be preserved, or the location of the evidence.

After the ruling made by the International Commercial Court is served on the parties, it shall notify the international commercial arbitration institution through the "One-Stop" Platform.

Article 23 Where an international commercial arbitration institution has made an arbitral award with respect to an international commercial dispute as specified in Article 2 of these Guidelines, and a party applies to the International Commercial Court for setting aside the domestic arbitral award or for recognition and enforcement of a foreign arbitral award, the party may, through the "Litigation Service" on the "One-Stop" Platform of the International Commercial Court, enter the "Supreme People's Court Litigation Service Network" and submit the following materials:

(1) A written application stating the basic information of the parties, the specific request and the facts and reasons on which it is based, and whether an application has already been filed with another court and the status of such application;

(2) The arbitral award;

(3) Identity certification materials;

(4) Where a lawyer or other person is entrusted to act as agent, the power of attorney and identity certification of the agent shall be submitted;

(5) Relevant evidentiary materials;

(6) Other materials required by the International Commercial Court.

Article 24 After receiving the materials for an application to set aside a domestic arbitral award or for recognition and enforcement of a foreign arbitral award, if the International Commercial Court considers that the dispute falls within the scope of application of Article 2 of these Guidelines, it shall register the case.

After accepting the case, the International Commercial Court shall form a collegiate panel to hear the case and question the parties. As needed for the trial of the case, the International Commercial Court may require the international commercial arbitration institution to provide explanations or consult the arbitration case file from the relevant arbitration institution.

The International Commercial Court shall render a ruling within two months from the date of acceptance of the case, and after the ruling is served on the parties, notify the international commercial arbitration institution through the "One-Stop" Platform.

Article 25 Where a party initiates litigation, it may, through the "Litigation Service" on the "One-Stop" Platform of the International Commercial Court, enter the "Supreme People's Court Litigation Service Network" and submit the statement of claim and related litigation materials.

The party may also submit the statement of claim and related litigation materials by email, mail, on-site submission, or other means permitted by the International Commercial Court.

If submitted by mail or on-site, the party shall provide paper documents and copies for the number of opposing parties, along with a CD or other portable mobile storage device.

Article 26 A party initiating litigation in the International Commercial Court shall submit the following materials:

(1) The statement of claim;

(2) A written agreement selecting the Supreme People's Court as the competent court;

(3) Identity certification materials;

(4) Where a lawyer or other person is entrusted to act as agent in the litigation, the power of attorney and identity certification of the agent shall be submitted;

(5) Relevant evidentiary materials in support of the claims;

(6) Confirmation of Service Address and Method;

(7) Pre-trial Diversion Procedure Consultation Form.

Article 27 After receiving the litigation materials submitted by the party, if the International Commercial Court considers that they fall within the scope of case acceptance as provided in Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of the International Commercial Court, it shall register the case online and send litigation materials such as the Notice of Acceptance of Case to the party through the "One-Stop" Platform.

Article 28 The International Commercial Court shall hear cases in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of the International Commercial Court, the Rules of the People's Court for Online Litigation, and other laws and judicial interpretations, as well as the Procedural Rules for the International Commercial Court of the Supreme People's Court (Trial).

Article 29 A party shall pay the case acceptance fee and other litigation costs in accordance with the provisions of the Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs.

The party may, using the payment code, pay the case acceptance fee and other litigation costs at any branch of the designated agent banks announced by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 30 The "One-Stop" Platform strictly complies with the relevant legal provisions on privacy protection, indicating the circumstances under which the Platform collects, stores, and uses the relevant information of the parties, as well as the relevant measures to ensure the confidentiality of mediation and arbitration.

Article 31 The "One-Stop" Platform provides, in a prominent position, the platform description, work guidelines, network environment requirements, etc., to facilitate parties in applying to use the platform services.

Neutral evaluation in these Guidelines refers to a dispute resolution mechanism in which, before a dispute is submitted to mediation, arbitration, or litigation, the parties jointly select a neutral third-party expert committee member to provide a professional evaluation opinion based on the circumstances of the case, enabling the parties to obtain sufficient information to assess the possible outcome of litigation and choose the most suitable dispute resolution method, thereby guiding and promoting the parties to prioritize mediation as the dispute resolution mechanism.

Identity certification materials in these Guidelines refer to, where a party is a natural person, the following shall be submitted: a copy of the identity card (for a foreign natural person, a copy of the passport; for a resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or the Macao Special Administrative Region, a copy of the identity card of the Hong Kong or Macao SAR, or a copy of the residence permit for Hong Kong or Macao residents, or a copy of the permit for Hong Kong or Macao residents to travel to and from the mainland; for a resident of the Taiwan region, a copy of the identity card of the Taiwan region, or a copy of the residence permit for Taiwan residents, or a copy of the permit for Taiwan residents to travel to and from the mainland, etc.).

When the party is a legal person or an unincorporated organization, it shall submit a copy of its registration certificate and a copy of the identity card of its legal representative or responsible person. A foreign enterprise or organization shall submit commercial registration certificates and identity certificates of its representative or responsible person, and other materials proving its status as a subject, which have been notarized by a notarial organ in the country where it is located, and authenticated by the Chinese embassy or consulate in that country, or that comply with the certification procedures stipulated in the relevant treaties concluded or jointly concluded between China and that country.

Article 32 These Guidelines shall take effect on January 30, 2024.
